acceptance.given: Success evaluation is requested while identity and execution facts may be unknown, missing, stale, ambiguous, or unverifiable.

oracle.expected: The success decision remains blocked unless both identity facts and execution facts are explicitly known and verifiable; a recorded success includes those facts.
forbidden: A success outcome is reported while identity or execution facts remain unknown.
Unknown or unverifiable facts are silently treated as known.
oracle.observable: A machine-readable semantic verdict or validation record showing identity_known=true and execution_facts_known=true for any success, with denial or block evidence for unknown inputs.

acceptance.then: The success predicate permits success only after both fact classes are known and verified.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run semantic verdict validation with identity facts omitted or marked unknown; expect the success predicate to reject or block the outcome.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require the semantic success gate to distinguish known, verified identity and execution facts from unknown, stale, ambiguous, or unverifiable values before allowing success.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve the existing verdict schema and fail-closed behavior; only tighten success eligibility.

slice_hint.state_transition: Unknown or unverifiable facts produce a blocked or non-success result; verified known facts become eligible for success evaluation.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: No success verdict is emitted unless identity and execution facts are both explicitly known and verified.

acceptance.given: The requested inspection target is illegal under the target-package validation rules.

oracle.expected: Target processing is rejected or halted before inspection or acceptance, with a machine-readable fail-closed result identifying the illegal target.
forbidden: Accepting an illegal target for inspection.
oracle.observable: The target validator returns a rejection or fail-closed status and no inspection acceptance is recorded.

acceptance.then: The illegal target is not accepted and processing has failed closed.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the target validator against an illegal target fixture and require rejection before any inspection result is accepted.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate target legality before inspection and fail closed for illegal target forms, preventing downstream acceptance.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Retain valid-target behavior and existing rejection status contract; tighten only illegal-target handling.

slice_hint.state_transition: Requested target -> legality check -> rejected or failed-closed for an illegal target.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: No illegal target reaches accepted inspection or processing.

acceptance.given: FR-3 validator verification is being performed and validator source, content, dependency closure, compatibility, support policy, and candidate-external trust are separate verification subjects.

oracle.expected: A verification record specifically evaluates validator source independently from the other FR-3 subjects.
forbidden: Validator source is treated as verified solely from verification of another aspect.
A combined pass record omits an explicit validator-source check.
oracle.observable: A machine-readable FR-3 verification artifact contains a dedicated validator_source assertion/result with its own evidence and pass or fail status.

acceptance.then: Validator source has an independently recorded verification result.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run FR-3 verification with validator-source evidence absent or replaced by content-only evidence; expect the dedicated validator_source check to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Add or enforce a dedicated validator-source verification assertion and evidence record independent of content, dependency, compatibility, policy, and trust checks.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep the existing FR-3 result envelope compatible while requiring an additional validator_source evidence member.

slice_hint.state_transition: FR-3 verification starts -> validator source independently checked -> dedicated result recorded.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: FR-3 cannot report validator verification complete without a dedicated validator_source result backed by source evidence.

acceptance.given: An Acceptance lifecycle owner is defined and an actor attempts to publish acceptance-passed.

oracle.expected: Only the current Acceptance lifecycle owner is authorized to publish acceptance-passed; every other actor is rejected, and the authorization decision is machine-verifiable.
forbidden: Publication succeeds without verifying that the actor is the current Acceptance lifecycle owner.
oracle.observable: The publication authorization record exposes an empty authorization set except for the current Acceptance lifecycle owner and records allow or deny outcomes for owner and non-owner attempts.

acceptance.then: Acceptance-passed publication is restricted to the current Acceptance lifecycle owner.
acceptance.when: When any actor attempts to publish acceptance-passed.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Attempt acceptance-passed publication as a non-owner and require denial; then attempt as the current lifecycle owner and require authorization only after owner identity verification.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce an explicit current Acceptance lifecycle-owner check for acceptance-passed publication and deny all other actors with a machine-verifiable authorization result.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve the existing publication artifact shape and lifecycle states; tighten authorization to the current Acceptance owner.

slice_hint.state_transition: Publication attempt -> resolve current Acceptance lifecycle owner -> allow only a matching actor, otherwise deny.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Exactly the current Acceptance lifecycle owner can produce acceptance-passed publication; all other actors are rejected.
